newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-Feb copper imports up 28 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-Feb copper imports up 28 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's total imports of unrefined copper and copper products in the first two months of 1997 were up 28.2 percent at 77,885 tonnes against the same period in 1996, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
Imports in February, however, were down 27.6 percent on imports in January, at 32,709 tonnes, the newspaper said.

Imports of unrefined copper, including alloys, were 10,587 tonnes in February, and totalled 18,869 tonnes in the first two months of the year, up 30.3 percent on the first two months of 1996, it said.

February's imports of copper scrap were 37,528 tonnes, down 2.1 percent on January, it said, adding that total copper scrap imports for the first two months of 1997 were 75,868 tonnes, up 10.8 percent on the same period in 1996.
The United States replaced Japan as China's biggest source of copper imports in Feburary 1997, the newspaper said.

Total copper imports from the United States in Feburary were 24,622 tonnes, with a cumulative total of 43,638 tonnes for the first two months of 1997, up 48.9 percent against the same period in 1996, it said.
China's copper imports from Japan in February were 12,926 tonnes, and for the first two months of the year 33,341 tonnes, up 28.7 percent on the same period in 1996, it said.

Most of China's copper imports arrived at ports in southern Guangdong province, totalling 29,289 tonnes in February and 77,255 tonnes for the first two months of the year, up 10.8 percent on the same period in 1996.
In February, 6,061 tonnes of copper arrived in Shanghai, and a total of 7,529 tonnes for January and February combined, up 61.7 percent on the same two-month period of 1996.
